FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finahzed by the Rotating Machinery Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. The brushes are used in electric machines operating on dc, ac or ac/dc systems. The in the country is sufficiently developed and the brush manufacturers found the existing mg in clearly specifying the requirements of brush material and ( in parts ) la c k' fabricated out of blocks. In the new approach it is decided to prepare the following existing parts of IS 3003. a) Definitions and nomenclature of carbon brushes, brush holders, commutators electrical machinery ( IS 13586 : 1992 ), b) Brush materials for electrical machinery c) Brushes for electrical machines Specification Specification ( IS 13466 : 1992 ). brush technology standard IS 3003 individual brushes standards out of and slip rings for

( IS 13584 : 1992 ), and

This standard is applicable to carbon brushes fabricated from carbon blocks ( see IS 13584 : 1992 ) and fttcd with its flexibles. The requirements specified earlier in 1S 3003 ( Part 3 ) : I978 and IS 3003 ( Part 4) : 1978 have been combined and updated in this standard. However, the methods of tests fog the following operational characteristics have been included in specification for brush m:\tcrinl f'ol- clcctrical machinery ( IS 13584 : 1992 ). a) Contact drop voltage, b) Coefficient of friction. and

The joints between tclminals and flcxiblo conductor shall be crimped or crimped and soldered as specified by the purchaser. 6.3 Current Carrying Thickness of Terminals Capacity and Minimum

This clause defines values of the current recommended in the flcxiblcs and the minimum thickness of terminals according to their cross section and sizes recommended for the terminals. In order to prevent small terminals being used with large section flexibles or vice versa, it is desirable to determine the current capacity fol each recommended terminal. Table I I gives the values which may be applied, hut higher values may bc used by agreement bctwcen the manuFacturer and the user. The current values given m Table I I correspond to the maximum section of one or scvcral flexihlc\ which may be flltcd correctly to a given terminal. These values relate to terminals with a rollctl or crrmpzd shank but 1w1 to terminals lnade from tubes or box terminal:, ( as shown in `F'ablc i0 ), which are nut included 111 this table. Offset A clip is similar to the Type A-extra wide clip cxccpt that the rivet is not placed at the centrc !ine of the brush ( see Fig. 3C ). 7.1.1.4 Extended A

7 CLIPS to as &clips' in this 7.1 Brush clips, referred standard, are metal parts attached to the brush which serve to accommodate the spring finger or hammer or to act as guides. Where these clips serve to prevent the,wear of the carbon due to the pressure finger, these are called `hammer' or ifinger' clips. Rotary converter brushes may have clips which serve the dual purpose of lifting the brushes and of preventing wear from the spring finger. These are generally called <lifting' clips.

Extended A clip is similar to th\: Type A ciip but extends beyond the side of the brush to accommodate the brush pressure finger ( see Fig. 3D ).

Angular A clip is similar to the Type A clip but is attached at an angle to accomplish the same purpose as bevelin, m the holder end of the brush ( see Fig. 3E ). 7.1.1.6 Channel A

TJ'his type is similar the edges turned
spring finger

to Type A except that it ]:;I\ up as a guide to position the OII top of the brush ( see Fig. 3E ).

ANNEX C ( Clause 16.2.1 )
SAMPLING C-l c-1.1 SAMPLING Lot PROCEDURE AND CRITERIA FOR ACCEPTANCE

In any consignment all the carbon brushes of the same designatron, manufactured from the same material under similar conditions of production shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. C-l.2 The number of brushes to be selected from each lot shall depend upon the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with columns 1, 2 and 3 of Table 16. These brushes shall be selected from the lot at random. In order to ensure randomness of seleclion, procedure given in 1s 4905 : 1968 shall be followed. C-2 CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY in 16 A The number of brushes selected at random accordance with co1 I and 2 of Table shall be subjected to all the acceptance tests. Table 16

brush failing to meet any of the requirements for acceptance tests shall be termed as defective. The lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of acceptance tests if the number of defectives found in the first sample is less than or equal to the corresponding acceptance number. The lot shall be rejected if the number of defectives is greater than or equal to the corresponding first rejection number ( see co1 5 of Table 16 ). If the number of defective is in between the acceptance number and the first rejection number, then a second sample of' the same size shall be selected from the lot at random and subjected to all the acceptance tests. The lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of acceptance tests, if the combined number of defectives in both the samples is less than the second rejection numbet ( see co1 6 of Table 16), otherwise not. and Rejection Numbers

( Cluuse 16.7.1 )
PROCEDURE FOR PULL-OUT STRENGTH TEST E-l EQUIPMENT
E-1.i The pull-out strength test device as shown in Fig. 16 shall be assembled. This comprises the following: A pulling device such that the tensile force to the flexible can be applisd at :I The maximum rate of uniform rate. increase should be 5 daN/s; A dynamometer for measuring the pullout strength with an accuracy of & 2.5 The measuring needle should percent. carry a dummy needle which should stop at the maximum value; Dash pot or any other d-vice to limit the shock at the moment of failure. This device should bc inoperative until the connection has failed; A gripping devics capabic of connecting the flexible of the brush to bc tested to the This should be capable of tension device. grippine the flexible adequately without damag&g its strength; and Adjustable support to ensure the lint of tensile force to be along the axis of the flexible. The support shall be capable of holding the brush without slipping and it should have a recess through which flexible can be passed. For information on such supports, see Fig. 17 and 18. E-2 TlXST YKOCEDURE E-2.1 Adju\l !he equipment as shown in Fig, 16 by placing a suitable support on the measuring dcvicc, laking into account the shape of the brush zncl the arlgle of the connection hole. Make sure that the tension is along the axis of the ilcxiblc. Also the hold on the brush should bz ho pl:~ccd that the brush will not break 01 crack or chip before the flexible is pulled out. E-2.2 Fix the flexible in the gripping flexible should be tested separately. device, each

E-2.3 Apply the force at a uniform rate without shock so that the connection fails in no1 les\ than 5 seconds after the force is first applied. E-2.4 After the failure of connection, read the maximum force indicated by the idle pointer. This force corresponds to the pull-out strength of the connection.

Guidance for selection and use of carbon brushes for electrical machines have been covered by 1s 9919 : 1981. In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from the following IEC Publications: of brushes and brush holders for electrical for determination machinery of carbon brushes of physical properties 1% Pub 136 ( 1986 ) Dimensions

IEC Pub 467 ( 1974 ) Test procedures for electrical machines

IEC Pub 773 ( 1983 ) Test methods and apparatus tics of brushes

for the measurements

of operational

characteris-

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Standard Mark The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, IY86 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may bc obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards;
